english: Let $Q=\dfrac{1}{3}\begin{pmatrix}1&2&2\\2&1&-2\\2&-2&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $X=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&1&-1\\2&0&1\end{pmatrix}$, and let $M=QX^{T}Q^{T}$, where $Y^{T}$ denotes the transpose of a matrix $Y$. Then the sum of the squares of all the entries of $M$ is
hindi: माना कि $Q=\dfrac{1}{3}\begin{pmatrix}1&2&2\\2&1&-2\\2&-2&1\end{pmatrix}$ तथा $X=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&1&-1\\2&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ है, और $M=QX^{T}Q^{T}$ है, जहाँ $Y^{T}$ आव्यूह $Y$ का परिवर्त (transpose) है। तब $M$ की सभी प्रविष्टियों के वर्गों का योग है
solution: For any square $Y$, the sum of squares of all entries of $Y$ equals $\mathrm{tr}\left(Y^{T}Y\right)$
Rows of $Q$ are unit vectors and mutually perpendicular, so $QQ^{T}=Q^{T}Q=I$ ($Q$ is orthogonal)
$\mathrm{tr}\left(M^{T}M\right)=\mathrm{tr}\left(XX^{T}Q^{T}Q\right)=\mathrm{tr}\left(XX^{T}\right)=$ sum of squares of entries of $X$ $=1+4+1+1+4+1=12$
solution_full: For any square matrix $Y=[y_{ij}]$, the $(j,j)$ entry of $Y^{T}Y$ is $\sum_i y_{ij}^{2}$, so $\mathrm{tr}\left(Y^{T}Y\right)=\sum_{i,j}y_{ij}^{2}$, the sum of the squares of all entries.

The rows of $Q$ are $\frac13(1,2,2)$, $\frac13(2,1,-2)$, $\frac13(2,-2,1)$. Each has length $\frac13\sqrt{1+4+4}=1$, and the dot products are $\frac19(2+2-4)=0$, $\frac19(2-4+2)=0$, $\frac19(4-2-2)=0$. Hence $QQ^{T}=I$, so $Q^{T}=Q^{-1}$ and $Q^{T}Q=I$.
$\mathrm{tr}\left(XX^{T}\right)$ is the sum of the squares of the entries of $X$: $1^{2}+2^{2}+0+0+1^{2}+(-1)^{2}+2^{2}+0+1^{2}=12$.
So the required sum is $12$ (a direct multiplication of the three matrices gives the same value).
originality_note: New: the sum of squares of the entries of Q X^T Q^T is shown to be independent of the orthogonal Q by writing it as tr(M^T M) (way 4, hidden invariant). Closest known: 'P orthogonal, Q = P A P^T, find P^T Q^n P'. Different because: no powers are involved; the question asks for an invariant (Frobenius norm) and the transpose of a triple product is the key step.

concept_use.Orthogonal matrices: Q is checked to be orthogonal (QQ^T = I), and Q^T Q = I cancels in M^T M.
concept_use.Transpose: properties and (AB)^T = B^T A: (Q X^T Q^T)^T = Q X Q^T by the reversal rule, and the sum of squares is written as tr(M^T M).
